chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from al-Jabbar ibn Ismail al-Rayyani from Yunus from a number of the companions of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

My father narrated to me from his forefathers from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever goes out on a journey and has with him a bitter almond stick and recites this verse—from His saying, 'And when he turned towards Madyan,' to His saying, 'And Allah is a Guardian over what we do'—Allah will protect him from every harmful beast, every thieving oppressor, and every creature with fever until he returns to his family and home, and seventy-seven angels will be with him seeking forgiveness for him until he returns and places it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits and protections for a traveler who recites this specific Quranic verse with a bitter almond stick?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the Shia tradition of combining physical amulets, specifically a bitter almond stick, with Quranic recitation for protection during travel. It underscores the concept of *mu'abbat* (guardian angels) who intercede for the believer, promising deliverance from beasts, thieves, and fever until the safe return home. This practice reflects the integration of tangible spiritual remedies with divine reliance (*tawakkul*) in Shia devotional life.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  narrates  from  his  predecessors, who narrate from Amirul Momineen (a.s.), who narrates that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “One who goes to a journey and   recites   the   verse:   Wa   lammaa   tawajjaha   tilqaa-a madyana…  till Allaahu  a’laa  maa  naqoolu  wakeel Allah will  protect  him  from  every  wild  animal,  thief,  oppressor and poisonous animals till he returns home.

This deed keeps poverty and Satan away. Once Adam (a.s.) became seriously ill  and  began  to  fear.  He  complained  about  it  to  Jibraeel (a.s.) who told him, ‘Take a branch of a bitter almond and keep it on your chest’. He did so and was relieved from the fear  by  Allah. One  who  wants  that the  distance  becomes short for him while traveling should carry a stick of bitter almond.”
